By way of instant appeal, appellant has assailed award dated 28.09.2015 passed by learned Motor Accident claims Tribunal-II, Solan in MACT petition No. 2-S/2 of 2013, whereby the claim petition of the petitioner has been dismissed..
2. Brief facts necessary for adjudication of the petition are that on 8.10.2011 vehicles bearing No.
HP-01S- Whether reporters of Local Papers may be allowed to see the judgment?
1015 (Alto car) and vehicle bearing No. CH-01Y-2886 (Tata 407) collided and place known as Koti near Railway Line Tunnel .

No.10 on N.H-5 at about 3.00P.M. Appellant (herein-after referred to as claimant) was driving Alto car No. HP-01S-1015 with two passengers, whereas the other vehicle bearing No. CH-01Y-2886 was being driven by respondent No.2.
of Claimant/Petitioner received injuries as a result of accident and suffered 30% permanent disability.

3. rt The claimant filed the claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicle Act, against the respondents with the allegation that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2.
Respondent No.1 and respondent No.3 were impleaded as insured and insurer of the offending vehicle respectively.

4. The claimant specifically alleged that while driving the Alto Car bearing No. HP-01S-1015 uphill,
one of the tyres of the vehicle punctured and the claimant had just parked the vehicle on the side of the road.

Before he could alight from the vehicle, the other vehicle bearing No. CH-01Y-2886 came from the opposite side and was being driven in a rash and negligent manner by respondent No.2 and hit against the parked vehicle of the petitioner causing injuries to the petitioner and other passengers in the vehicle.

. 
5. Respondents No. 1 and 2 contested the claim petition of the claimant by filing their joint reply.
The averments made in the petition were denied in general terms.
The allegations of rashness and negligence against respondent No.2 were of specifically denied, however, no details were provided as to how the accident had taken place.
6. rt Respondent No.3 the insurer also contested the claim petition on the grounds that the driver of the vehicle was not holding valid driving licence at the time of accident.
Counter allegations of rashness and negligence were levelled against the claimant.

It was averred that the claimant was driving the vehicle in rash and negligent manner and while overtaking another vehicle on the road,
the vehicle driven by claimant was of the wrong side of the road, which resulted in the collision of the vehicles.
It was also submitted that the FIR was also lodged against the petitioner.

Even the Mandeep Alias Nikka vs Ravi Kumar And Ors on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37228943/
2 claimant was alleged to be driving the vehicle without any driving licence.

sentences.text: 7. On the basis of pleadings of the parties, learned Tribunal framed following issues.

1. Whether the petitioner sustained injuries on account of rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2 of vehicle bearing No. CH-01Y-2886 dated 08.10.2011 at about 3:00 PM at place Kothi near Railway Tunnel No.10, as alleged?
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom?
...OPP 3. Whether the petition is not maintainable?
Whether the respondent No.2 was not having valid and effective driving licence?
...OPR3 of 5.Whether the vehicle in question was being plied in violation of the terms and conditions of the policy?
Whether rt the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties?OPR3 7. Relief.
8. All the issues except issue No.2 were decided in negative.
Issue No.2 was partially decided in affirmative.

The claimant was held entitled to a sum of Rs.
25,000/- only on account of no fault liability, rest of the claim of the petitioner was denied by dismissal of the petition.

9. I have heard Mr.O.C.Sharma, learned counsel for the petitioner and Mr. Aditya and Mr. Sanjay Sharma, Advocates for respondents No. 1& 2 and 3 respectively and have also gone through the relevant record.
10. The reasons for dismissal of the claim petition filed by claimant have been rendered by learned Tribunal in para 21 of the impugned award.

Learned Tribunal has held the evidence led on behalf of the claimant to be unworthy of credit on the basis of some difference in the statement of the .
witness of the claimant PW-4 Rasool Khan while deposing before learned Tribunal as against his deposition made before the criminal Court, in a case where the claimant was charged for offences under Sections 279 and 337 of Indian Penal Code of for the same incident.

Learned Tribunal took notice of the fact that while deposing before the criminal Court PW-4 Rasool rt Khan had not stated about the factum of vehicle having been parked by claimant on account of puncture of the tyre.

Further, learned Tribunal placed reliance on the judgment passed in the criminal case Ext. PW3/B to infer that the claimant, in the criminal case, had also not taken a stand with respect to the puncture of the tyre of vehicle as a reason for parking of the vehicle on the side of the road.

On the Mandeep Alias Nikka vs Ravi Kumar And Ors on 14 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/37228943/
3 strength of above reasons, learned Tribunal did not find any material to hold that the accident was caused by rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2.
11. PW-4 Rasool Khan in his evidence/affidavit Ext.
PW4/A had specifically stated that he was travelling alongwith the claimant in vehicle bearing No.
HP-01S-1015.

sentences.text: When the vehicle reached near Koti, claimant was driving the vehicle on his side in controlled speed.

The tyre of the vehicle of claimant got punctured abruptly and the claimant for such .
reason was about to park the vehicle on the side of the road, respondent No.2 came driving the vehicle CH-01Y-2886 from the other side in wrong direction and struck against the vehicle of claimant.
He had also attributed the cause of the accident of to the rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2.
This witness, during cross-examination, was not confronted with rt his statement on oath recorded before the criminal Court.

12. A few questions were asked from this witness in cross-examination on behalf of respondents No.
1 and 2, whereby he was tried to be confronted with his previous statement made to the police under Section 161 of Cr.P.C, that too without confronting him with the contents of the statement.

Thus,
learned Tribunal was not at all justified to return findings on question of fact on legally inadmissible evidence.
Without affording the witness Rasool Khan an opportunity to explain his statement given before trial Court, the same could not have been relied upon.

Further, learned trial Court placed reliance upon contents of judgment passed by criminal Court to hold that claimant had not taken same stand before criminal Court, which he had taken in the claim petition.
Such finding, in my considered view, is highly illegal and perverse.
Claimant was an accused before the criminal .
Court.
It is beyond comprehension that how learned Tribunal could ascertain the defence of the accused from the judgment of criminal Court, in which he was acquitted.
The learned Tribunal had to decide the issues before it on the strength of of merits of the evidence led before it.

It was not to be guided by the contents of judgment passed by the criminal Court, the rt contents of the judgment of criminal Court could not have been relied upon as evidence in the case against the claimant.
In view of what has been held above, the impugned award on findings on issues No. 1 and 2 cannot be sustained.
While, deciding issues No. 4 and 5, learned Tribunal has held the same against respondent No.3/ insurer.
There is no challenge to such findings.
13. Noticeably, except by way of cross examining, the witnesses of claimant, respondents had led no evidence.

From the statement of claimant who appeared as PW-3 and corroborated by the statement of PW-4 Rasool Khan, the cause of accident has clearly been proved to be rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2.
It is not the case that PW-4 Rasool Khan was a planted witness.
The respondents have rather admitted this fact in their replies.
Even the contents of FIR Ex. PW1/A suggest that claimant was accompanied by two .

4 passengers in the vehicle at the time of accident.

sentences.text: The presence of PW-4 Rasool Khan on the spot at the time of accident has not been challenged by either of the respondent while cross- examining this witness.

Since, the factum of accident being of result of rash and negligent driving of respondent No.2 was proved by preponderance of evidence coupled with the fact rt that no breach of the terms of the policy of insurance of offending vehicle was found, the claimant is entitled to compensation from respondents.
14.
It is not in dispute that the claimant was a driver by profession and at the time of accident was driving a commercial vehicle i.e. a cab.
Claimant has been able to prove that as a result of injuries suffered in the accident, he has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 30 per cent.

PW-2 Dr.
J.L. Sharma, has proved the issuance of disability certificate Ext. PW2/A in favour of the claimant.
Perusal of the contents of disability certificate reveal that a Board of experts had examined the claimant and had thereafter issued the certificate of disability.
The percentage of disability has been certified to be 30 percent with the findings of fracture of pelvis (right).
It has also been mentioned that claimant was unable to squat and cross his legs.

Nothing contrary could be elicited by the .
respondents from the statement of PW-2.
Thus, it was duly proved that the petitioner has suffered 30 percent disability.
15. Learned counsel for the claimant had contended that the claimant had not been able to drive the vehicle since the of time of accident and has virtually been rendered jobless.
The statements made by the claimant has to be considered in rt light of other evidence on record.
In his examination-in-chief, PW-2 had stated that after the disability, as suffered by claimant, a person will not be able to drive comfortably.
While being cross-examined on this aspect, PW-2 admitted that the claimant could drive the vehicle though he would not be comfortable.

Since, PW-2 was witness of the claimant and in his examination-in-chief itself, said witness stated that the person with disability as described in Ext. PW2/A would not be completely disabled from driving the vehicle.

The petitioner has not led any further evidence to prove his complete inability to drive the vehicle after the accident except for his bald statement, no cogent and reliable evidence was brought on record.
The evidence of PW-2 no doubt was an opinion and the Court is not bound by such opinion,

however, in absence of any cogent material to the contrary on record, this Court is not in a position to hold that the claimant/petitioner was .
completely disabled from driving the vehicle after the accident.
16. In a result, it is held that the petitioner has suffered 30 percent disability as a result of accident.
The age of the petitioner at the time of accident is stated to be 40 years, of which fact has also not been denied by the respondent.
The claimant claimed to be earning Rs. 10,000/- P.M by plying rt the aforesaid car.

As per his own case, the petitioner was owner-cum-driver of the Alto car(Taxi)
bearing No. HP-01S- 1015.
In his affidavit claimant has also stated that income to be Rs. 10,000/- P.M at the time of accident.

In his evidence also the claimant has stated his income to be Rs. 10,000/-

5 P.M at the time of accident.

sentences.text: In his cross examination, no serious attempt has been made to discredit his version about his earning.
As noticed above, respondents have not led any evidence.
The income of Rs.10,000/- P.M by self employed driver-cum-owner in the year 2011 cannot be said to be excessive.
In this view of matter, the monthly income of claimant for the purposes assessment of compensation is taken at Rs. 10,000/-.
In the given circumstances, the loss of income on account of the disability suffered by the claimant can reasonably be said to be corresponding to the percentage of disability suffered.

Therefore, the loss of income to the .
petitioner /claimant will be Rs. 3,000/- P.M.
The age of the claimant was 40 years and thus multiplier of 15 will be relevant.

Accordingly the loss of income of claimant can be assessed at Rs.
3,000/- X12 X 15 = 5,40,000.
of 17.

In addition the claimant has also proved on record certain bills/voucher evidencing the expenses on account of medicines rt and laboratory tests etc. Exts. P-1to P-20 reveal total expenses of Rs.27,000/- to which petitioner is also entitled.
18. Further, petitioner has proved that he had remained admitted at PGI, Chandigarh from 10.10.2011 to 17.10.2011 and for one day i.e. on 9.10.2011, he had remained in CHC hospital Parwanoo.
The petitioner is resident of Dharampur in Solan District of Himachal Pradesh.
In such circumstances, it can easily be assumed that petitioner must have been attended by a few attendants in the hospital during period of his admission as indoor patient.
Taking into account their daily expenses besides journey undertaken by them as also the special diet for claimant, award of sum of Rs. 25,000/- will not be unreasonable.

In addition, petitioner is also held entitled to a sum of Rs.
20,000/- on account of pain and agony suffered by him.
In this manner petitioner is entitled for the .

following:-
On account of loss of income Rs. 5,40,000/-

On account of medical Rs. 27,000/-
 expenses  of

On account of hospital Rs. 25,000/-

rt  On account of pain and agony Rs. 20,000/-

20. The respondents shall be jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount, however, since there is no challenge to the findings recorded by learned Tribunal on issues Nos. 4 and 5, the liability to pay the compensation amount shall be on respondent No.3, Insurer.
21. In light of above discussions, the appeal is allowed in aforesaid terms and is accordingly disposed of, so also the .
